dedupe_keys.name: san francisco mandatory soft story retrofit program wood frame multi unit buildings

description: San Francisco's Mandatory Soft Story Retrofit Program, signed into law on the anniversary of the 1906 earthquake in April 2013, requires seismic retrofit of multi-unit soft-story buildings: wood-frame structures with five or more residential units, two or more stories over a soft or weak story, and a construction permit application before 1 January 1978. The city's ESIP page gathers the ordinance and its amendments to Building Code Chapter 34B, administrative bulletins on implementation and engineering criteria, financing and tenant passthrough rules, liquefaction guidance, and the CAPSS and ATC 52-3 research that motivated the programme, with a status lookup for each building. The Office of Resilience and Capital Planning notes about 5,000 buildings, housing roughly 180,000 residents, with deadlines between 2017 and 2020. Coverage: San Francisco. Access: city web pages and documents. Licence: website content, no licence stated; free to read. Caveats: the ESIP page was last revised in 2016, and current compliance counts were not on the pages read. Simulation uses are as a reference for mandatory retrofit policy, regional seismic loss reduction and housing displacement studies. Related records: the California Earthquake Brace + Bolt programme.
